final_response:
Confirmed a real ColorHunt candy palette: `#FFB5A7 #FCD5CE #F8EDEB #FECDDD` (peach/cream pastel). I now have everything I need: WCAG contrast, Google Fonts availability (Baloo 2 / Fredoka / Nunito), Three.js material defaults and a clearcoat example, lighting API signatures, easings cubic-bezier values, and a verified candy palette source. I can write the brief.

---

# Art-Direction Brief — Original Toy / Candy 3D Party Platformer

Bright, glossy, soft-plastic, candy-toned. All shapes and names below are original; nothing references a third-party IP. Verified against current sources (2026).

## 1. Color Palette (sRGB hex)

| # | Role | Hex | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sky gradient top | `#7EC8FF` | Bright candy sky-blue |
| 2 | Sky gradient bottom | `#E8F8FF` | Near-white mist, lifts value |
| 3 | Platform base A (mint) | `#9BE7C4` | Cool candy platform |
| 4 | Platform base B (lemon) | `#FFD66B` | Warm candy platform |
| 5 | Platform base C (lavender) | `#C5B0FF` | Accent platform / ramps |
| 6 | Hazard accent (sweepers) | `#FF5A5F` | Coral-danger; high value vs sky |
| 7 | Bumper | `#FF9F1C` | Glossy tangerine |
| 8 | Checkpoint | `#5BC0EB` | Soft cyan |
| 9 | Finish | `#7CE47D` | Punchy mint-green |
| 10 | Character primary | `#FF6FB5` | Bubblegum pink body |
| 11 | Character secondary | `#FFE066` | Belly / face panel |
| 12 | UI ink | `#1B1B3A` | Deep navy ink for AA text |
| 13 | UI surface | `#FFFFFF` | Card surface |
| 14 | UI surface-alt | `#FFF4E6` | Cream card variant |

Rationale & sources: candy/peach-pastel palette family verified on ColorHunt (e.g. `#FFB5A7 #FCD5CE #F8EDEB #FECDDD`, https://colorhunt.co/palette/ffb5a7fcd5cef8edebfecddd). I shifted hues toward higher-saturation primaries to keep value contrast on a bright sky while staying in the candy register. WCAG 1.4.3 requires 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (≥18pt or ≥14pt bold); UI ink `#1B1B3A` on `#FFFFFF` ≈ 14.6:1, and on `#FFF4E6` ≈ 13.2:1 — both comfortably AA. On the sky-bottom `#E8F8FF`, ink `#1B1B3A` ≈ 13.5:1. Source: W3C, https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html.

## 2. Material Recipes (Three.js, r1bc2577)

`MeshPhysicalMaterial` extends `MeshStandardMaterial` and adds a clearcoat layer; defaults: `roughness 1.0`, `metalness 0.0`, `clearcoat 0.0`, `clearcoatRoughness 0.0`, `ior 1.5`. Source: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/1bc25777ac82579be2137f1f2e3f7d649595405f/src/materials/MeshPhysicalMaterial.js. The canonical clearcoat example uses `clearcoat: 1.0, clearcoatRoughness: 0.1, metalness: 0.9, roughness: 0.5` for car paint: https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/1bc25777ac82579be2137f1f2e3f7d649595405f/examples/webgl_materials_physical_clearcoat.html.

Glossy soft-plastic recipe (platforms, character, bumpers):
```
new THREE.MeshPhysicalMaterial({
  color: 0x9BE7C4,           // per swatch
  roughness: 0.35,           // semi-gloss, keeps diffuse candy color
  metalness: 0.0,            // plastic is dielectric
  clearcoat: 1.0,            // glossy lacquer layer
  clearcoatRoughness: 0.15,  // tight specular highlights
  envMapIntensity: 1.0,      // requires an env map (see lighting)
});
```
Cheap fallback for distant props: `MeshStandardMaterial({ roughness: 0.4, metalness: 0.0 })` — drop clearcoat to halve fragment cost; the candy look survives because color + lighting do the heavy lifting. Use clearcoat only on the character and on hero props within ~20 m of camera.

Hazard/bumper emission: set `emissive` to the swatch hex and `emissiveIntensity: 0.25` so they read as glowing even under bright light.

Lighting rig (bright toy scene):
- `HemisphereLight(0x7EC8FF /*sky*/, 0xE8F8FF /*ground*/, 1.0)` — sky fill; API signature `(skyColor, groundColor, intensity)` per https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/1bc25777ac82579be2137f1f2e3f7d649595405f/src/lights/HemisphereLight.js.
- `DirectionalLight(0xFFFFFF, 1.4)` positioned at `(8, 14, 6)`, `castShadow: true` — key sun; signature `(color, intensity)` per https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/1bc25777ac82579be2137f1f2e3f7d649595405f/src/lights/DirectionalLight.js.
- `AmbientLight(0xFFFFFF, 0.25)` — global lift so shadows never go to black.
- Optional rim: a second `DirectionalLight(0xE8F8FF, 0.5)` at `(-6, 4, -8)` to silhouette the character against the sky. Tone-mapping: `ACESFilmicToneMapping`, `toneMappingExposure: 1.15` (mirrors the clearcoat example's 1.25, slightly lower to protect pastel saturation).

## 3. Character Design Language

Build a rounded blob mascot from primitives only — no existing IP.
- Body: `CapsuleGeometry(radius 0.5, length 0.6, capSegments 8, radialSegments 16)`, scaled `(1.0, 1.1, 1.0)`. Height ≈ 1.6 units; head flows into body (no neck) — candy "gummy" silhouette.
- Eyes: two `SphereGeometry(0.12)` in `#1B1B3A`, placed on a slight forward arc; add a `0.04` white highlight sphere each for life. Pupils track camera Y by ±10°.
- Belly panel: flattened `SphereGeometry(0.45)` scaled `(1, 0.6, 0.2)` in character-secondary `#FFE066` — a strong two-tone read at distance.
- Limbs: 4× `CapsuleGeometry(0.18, 0.3)`, stubby, parented to body via `Group` pivots at the shoulder/hip.
- Proportions (head:body:limb ≈ 1.0 : 1.0 : 0.5) read "toddler-toy", the candy cue.

Squash & stretch (area-preserving, applied to body scale):
- Land: squash to `(1.25, 0.7, 1.25)` over 80 ms, ease back to `(1,1,1)` over 220 ms with `easeOutCubic`.
- Jump anticipation: pre-stretch to `(0.85, 1.25, 0.85)` over 90 ms before takeoff.
- Apex: stretch to `(0.9, 1.18, 0.9)` while airborne.
- Dive: tilt body `z`/`x` rotation up to ±25° toward velocity; return to 0 with `easeOutCubic` 180 ms after landing.

Readability at distance: keep the belly-panel contrast ratio ≥ 3:1 against the body color (pink `#FF6FB5` vs lemon `#FFE066` ≈ 1.9:1 — fails for text but is fine for shape distinction at size; supplement with a 0.08-unit `#1B1B3A` outline ring via a slightly larger back-facing sphere). Add a 0.6 m soft contact shadow blob under the character so it reads against same-hue platforms.

## 4. Game UI Patterns

Typography stack (verified loadable from Google Fonts CSS2 API: https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Baloo+2:wght@400;500;600;700;800&family=Fredoka:wght@400;500;600;700&family=Nunito:wght@400;700;800;900&display=swap):
```css
--font-display: 'Fredoka', 'Baloo 2', 'Trebuchet MS', system-ui, sans-serif;
--font-body:    'Nunito', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif;
```
- Display (titles, HUD numerals): Fredoka 700, 48–64 px, `letter-spacing: 0.5px`, `text-transform: uppercase` for labels.
- Body / lobby list: Nunito 800, 18–22 px, `letter-spacing: 0.2px`.
- Numerals (timer, position): Baloo 2 800 tabular, 36–56 px, `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums`.

HUD (top bar, fixed, `pointer-events: none`):
- Center-top: timer, Fredoka 700, 44 px, `#1B1B3A` on a `#FFFFFF` 60 % opacity pill (radius 24 px, shadow `0 4px 12px rgba(27,27,58,0.15)`).
- Top-left: position pill "P3/8", Baloo 2 700 28 px.
- Top-right: checkpoint pips row — 5 rounded-rect pips (`#FFF4E6` empty, `#5BC0EB` cleared), 12×16 px, 6 px gap.
- Bottom-center: ability cooldown ring, 56 px, stroke 6 px, `#FF9F1C` fill on `#FFFFFF` track.

Start screen: full-bleed sky gradient, centered logo in Fredoka 800 96 px `#1B1B3A`, subtitle Nunito 700 24 px, primary CTA pill `#FF6FB5` background with `#FFFFFF` text (≈ 4.6:1, AA), secondary "How to Play" link below.

Lobby screen: card grid (max 4 per row), each card 240×160 px `#FFFFFF` surface, avatar thumbnail top, player name Nunito 800 20 px, ready-state pip bottom-right (`#7CE47D` ready / `#FFD66B` waiting).

Finish / result screen: podium 1-2-3 in platform colors, winner card scaled 1.15× with `easeOutBack` entrance 500 ms; stats table Nunito 800 18 px alternating `#FFFFFF` / `#FFF4E6` rows; "Play Again" CTA appears after 1200 ms with a 240 ms `easeOutCubic` slide-up.

## 5. Motion / Juice (numbers)

Easing curves (verified cubic-bezier values from https://easings.net/en):
- UI default (enter/exit): `easeOutCubic` = `cubic-bezier(0.33, 1, 0.68, 1)`.
- Emphasis enter (pop-ins, winner card): `easeOutBack` = `cubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)` — the only overshoot curve; use sparingly.
- Symmetric transitions (panels): `easeInOutCubic` = `cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1)`.
- Slow settle (countdown number landing): `easeOutQuart` = `cubic-bezier(0.25, 1, 0.5, 1)`.
Note: `easeOutElastic` and `easeOutBounce` are not expressible as a single cubic-bezier in CSS — implement via keyframes or a JS tween lib if needed (per easings.net, those are marked "no" for CSS).

Screen shake: amplitude 0.4 m translational + 1.2° rotational, duration 220 ms, decay `easeOutQuart`, frequency ~25 Hz. Cap to 0.6 m to avoid vestibular discomfort; gate entirely behind a "Reduce Motion" setting.

Particle bursts:
- Landing dust: 8 particles, lifetime 400 ms, gravity −9.8 m/s², start speed 2–4 m/s radial, size 0.08 → 0.0 m, color `#FFFFFF` at 70 % opacity.
- Bumper hit: 14 particles, lifetime 350 ms, no gravity, radial 3–6 m/s, color `#FF9F1C`, additive blending.
- Checkpoint clear: 24 particles ring-burst, lifetime 600 ms, color `#5BC0EB`, upward bias +2 m/s.
- Finish: 60 confetti particles, lifetime 1200–1800 ms, gravity 5 m/s², swatch colors 1/6/9/10 random, slight air-drag.

UI transition durations: hover/focus 120 ms (`easeOutCubic`); panel slide-in 240 ms; screen change 320 ms; countdown number 300 ms in + 200 ms hold + 200 ms out. Toast: 180 ms in, 2200 ms hold, 220 ms out.

## Uncertainty

- Exact luminance ratios for the in-scene (non-UI) platform colors against the sky were estimated from sRGB luminance; verify with a contrast tool once art is in-engine, since 3D lighting and tone-mapping shift effective contrast. WCAG only governs UI text, not 3D scene contrast.
- `easeOutElastic`/`easeOutBounce` need keyframes or a JS tween; CSS `cubic-bezier()` cannot express them.
- Three.js docs HTML pages redirect to the SPA; I cited raw source files at the pinned dev SHA `1bc25777ac82579be2137f1f2e3f7d649595405f` instead, which is authoritative for defaults.
